The drum kit is an instrument made of several percussion instruments combined, played by a single drummer, of the membranophone class, Hornbostel–Sachs 211.212.21. Its usual parts include snare drum, bass drum, tom-toms, cymbals and hi-hat, sometimes with auxiliary percussion such as tambourine and cowbell. The drummer usually sits on a stool, strikes with sticks or brushes, and works the bass drum and hi-hat with pedals. It is used in the rhythm section of pop, rock, blues, jazz and other music, and also in musical-theatre bands and similar settings.
